threats.title: SQL injection in login
threats.description: TOP 5. L5 x I5 = 25. An attacker can type special text in the login box and log in without knowing the password.
threats.mitigation: Use a parameterized query for login. Also store hashed passwords, not plain text.

threats.title: Forged session cookie
threats.description: L3 x I4 = 12. The secret key is written in the code, so an attacker can make a fake login cookie and pretend to be a rider.
threats.mitigation: Keep the secret key in an environment variable and use a long random value. (D4 Secrets)

threats.title: Brute force on login
threats.description: L4 x I3 = 12. There was no limit on login attempts, so an attacker could try thousands of passwords.
threats.mitigation: Limit login attempts to 5 per minute. Block the user for a while after too many failures. (C1 Limiter)

threats.title: Unlock without login
threats.description: TOP 5. L5 x I5 = 25. On flow F3, anyone could call /unlock without logging in and open a bike.
threats.mitigation: Check that the user is logged in before unlocking. Also check that the bike belongs to the rider's ride. (C2 Auth gate)

threats.title: Errors reveal internals
threats.description: L4 x I3 = 12. Debug mode and raw error messages showed internal details to the attacker.
threats.mitigation: Turn debug off. Show a simple message like "Something went wrong" and save the real error in a server log.

threats.title: Rider acts as operator
threats.description: L4 x I4 = 16. On flow F6, a normal rider could call /refund because there was no role check.
threats.mitigation: Save the user's role (rider or operator) at login and check it on /refund. (C2 Auth gate)

threats.title: Refund has no audit log
threats.description: L3 x I3 = 9. Refunds were not recorded, so nobody could prove who gave a refund.
threats.mitigation: Write a log line for every refund with the time, operator id and ride id. (D3 Audit log)

threats.title: Read other riders' rides
threats.description: TOP 5. L5 x I4 = 20. A rider can change the number in the URL and see another rider's rides.
threats.mitigation: Use the logged-in rider's id from the session, not from the URL. Return 403 if not logged in. (C2 Auth gate)

threats.title: Lock API key stolen
threats.description: TOP 5. L4 x I5 = 20. The lock API key is written in the code, so anyone who sees the code can unlock bikes.
threats.mitigation: Keep the key in an environment variable, not in the code. (D4 Secrets)

threats.title: Slow lock service freezes backend
threats.description: L3 x I4 = 12. The lock request has no timeout, so if the lock service is slow, the whole backend freezes.
threats.mitigation: Add a timeout of 3 seconds to the lock request. If it fails, show a simple error message.

threats.title: Anyone can refund any ride
threats.description: TOP 5. L5 x I4 = 20. Anyone can call /refund and set a ride's cost to 0. The code does not check who is calling.
threats.mitigation: Allow /refund only for logged-in operators. Return 403 for everyone else. (C2 Auth gate)
